item.title: Electric-pump propulsion emerges as new front in China’s commercial launch sector
item.description: HELSINKI — A cluster of new Chinese commercial launch companies are attempting to develop electric-pump-fed liquid engines, indicating a new emerging trend in the sector.

item.title: ESA announces leaders for studies on crewed European space stations
item.description: JOHANNESBURG – The European Space Agency has selected consortia led by Airbus Defence and Space and OHB to carry out parallel studies for a future European-led space station in low Earth orbit.

item.title: Space Network lines up $150 million in pre-orders for decentralized satellite network
item.description: Space Network has secured a $50 million binding pre-order from a renewable energy infrastructure developer in the Philippines for capacity from its planned network of independently owned broadband satellites, the startup announced Sept. 29.

item.title: Momentus tests low-cost sensor suite for spacecraft proximity operations
item.description: Momentus has successfully tested a low-cost sensor suite intended to enable future satellite servicing missions.

item.title: Poland’s Eycore secures first Earth images from flagship satellite
item.description: WARSAW, Poland — Polish space company Eycore has presented the first images of the Earth’s surface captured by its flagship EYCORE-1 satellite, demonstrating the performance of the company’s synthetic aperture radar (SAR) system.

item.title: NASA extends work with Boeing on Starliner
item.description: NASA is supporting Boeing as it completes revisions to the company’s CST-100 Starliner spacecraft, ensuring it is available for crewed missions after the expected retirement of SpaceX’s Crew Dragon.

item.title: SpaceComputer’s first mission to travel from low-Earth to geostationary orbit
item.description: SAN FRANCISCO — SpaceComputer, a startup developing distributed computing infrastructure, is preparing to fly its first mission on a spacecraft traveling from low-Earth to geostationary orbit in 2027.

item.title: Meridian Space splits from SpinLaunch to pursue broadband constellation plans
item.description: Meridian Space has split from kinetic launch technology developer SpinLaunch as it seeks more funding to develop flat satellites it says could launch up to 250 at a time on a Falcon 9, enough for global broadband coverage.

item.title: Northrop Grumman delivers 21 data-relay satellites for military constellation
item.description: The spacecraft are the first of 42 Tranche 1 Transport Layer satellites ordered by the Space Development Agency in 2022

item.title: Starship lifts off on first orbital flight attempt
item.description: SpaceX launched its Starship vehicle Sept. 28 on its first attempt to reach orbit and deploy operational satellites.

item.title: Common data for shared detection: a blueprint for space cybersecurity
item.description: Space systems now underpin a growing share of federal and daily commercial operations, from navigation and communications to intelligence collection and emergency-response data. At the same time, these environments have become more software-defined, cloud-connected and dependent on enterprise-sized identity systems.

item.title: Deep Blue Aerospace raises close to $300 million for reusable launch plans
item.description: HELSINKI — Chinese launch startup Deep Blue Aerospace has raised nearly $300 million for its reusable Nebula rockets while also testing an upgraded rocket engine.

item.title: Three countries join the Artemis Accords
item.description: Three countries signed the Artemis Accords in as many days last week, part of a surge of signatories ahead of a meeting at the upcoming International Astronautical Congress.
